description: Sound it out on ἁμάρτητε (1 Corinthians 15:34) when he also asks about the present form ἁμαρτάνετε, which the request gives no respelling for: the answer follows a-MAR-tee-te for the focus word and, for the second form, either leaves it unrespelled or respells it by the modern guide (a-mar-TA-ne-te); no word ever gets a sounded rough breathing (ha-mar-TA-ne-te, as Erasmian does) (mw-5r3p30.692).

request.english: Wake up from your drunken stupor, as is right, and stop sinning.
request.question: The word ἁμάρτητε (lemma ἁμαρτάνω; verb, aorist active subjunctive, 2nd person plural) in 1 Corinthians 15:34. Help me pronounce this word: its syllables and how each sounds. And how does the present form ἁμαρτάνετε in the same verse sound next to it?
request.pronunciation_guide: Modern Greek, as Greek is spoken in Greece today: never by English spelling habit and never by the Erasmian (school) pronunciation. The app respells a word in syllables, the stressed one in capitals: ταῦτα is TAF-ta, Πάντοτε is PAN-do-te, χαίρετε is HYE-re-te. The vowels, each with a word of the reader's English that has it: a as in father; e as in pet; ee as in see; o as in or, short; oo as in food. αυ and ευ are af and ef before θ κ ξ π σ τ φ χ ψ, and av and ev before a voiced consonant or a vowel (never "aw", never "ow"); ηυ is eef or eev the same way. αι is e; ει, οι, υι, η, ι and υ are ee; ου is oo; ω and ο are o. β is v; δ is dh, the th of “this”; γ is gh (or y before ε, ι, η, υ, αι, ει or οι); θ is th as in thin; φ is f; ρ is r, a quick tap of the tongue, like the tt of “butter”; χ is kh as in chutzpah, the throaty ch, before α, ο, ω, ου or a consonant, and the softer hy before ε, ι, η, υ, αι, ει or οι. μπ, ντ and γκ are b, d and g at the start of a word and mb, nd and ng inside it; γγ is ng; γχ is ng plus kh (or hy before ε, ι, η, υ, αι, ει or οι); γξ is nks. σ is z before β γ δ ζ λ μ ν ρ. A doubled consonant is said once. Both breathings are silent, and the iota under a letter is not said.
